scope: Current physical-print effects and paper rules; no executable/native engine claims
interpretation: fixed is an authored printed effect change; keep is an intentional legal restriction, trade-off, or alternate line of play; all 14 have targeted regression scenarios, not win-rate evidence

cases.reason: Frontline-only Forces compete for the same position and both apply Shaken (which does not stack). Move Duelists away if sequential deployment is wanted; there is no automatic payoff for chaining them.
cases.gameplay_decision: Both may be drawn, but they cannot simultaneously occupy one Frontline. It is a choice between a Skirmisher and a Raider deployment, not a two-card buff.

cases.reason: Kept Pace With grants Move, not Maneuver; Grey Riders' optional post-Maneuver Attack must not trigger.
cases.gameplay_decision: Choose between card-enabled tempo Move and an ordinary Maneuver with potential free Attack. A separate normal Attack still needs an Action.

cases.card_b: No One Would Be First to Leave
cases.reason: The Narrative's ACTION moves formations; it does not grant Maneuvers. Grey Riders' post-Maneuver Attack does not trigger.
cases.gameplay_decision: Recovery and coordinated Moves are different from paying for a Maneuver, even though both reposition formations.

cases.reason: Dust Riders' first Bonded normal Maneuver and The Long March both save its one Command; cost cannot go below zero. A printed ACTION Move is not a Maneuver.
cases.gameplay_decision: Long March continues to help subsequent Rider Maneuvers and other Riders; Dust can be useful without drawing the Narrative.

cases.reason: Opening Maneuvers are already free of Command. Long March does not further discount them; the Bond still adds one legal Move.
cases.gameplay_decision: Meaningful trade-off: a Bonded formation's additional positioning versus spending normal-turn Actions/Command for ordinary Rider Maneuvers.

cases.reason: PLAY occurs when the Bond is prepared. House of Reed moving it into an existing Force can complete Named but never replays PLAY +2.
cases.gameplay_decision: Players can choose direct-play Strength burst or a prepared-layer assembly route; the latter may still trigger Name completion and Guarded from House.

cases.reason: Crow Archers extend ordinary Archer targeting to Middle only while opposing Frontline is empty. Every Bow Was Strung permits a Bonded Archer's Opening Strike to target Middle even when occupied.
cases.gameplay_decision: The Narrative is a situational bypass, not a second Attack. Preserve the difference between a permanent gap ability and a Battle-specific opening plan.

cases.reason: The Line Was Baited is a Tactic, not the Skirmisher's own marker source. The Trap Closed now expressly includes a Tactic played while its controller has a Raider/Skirmisher in the assigned Front.
cases.gameplay_decision: Trigger only after a legal rearward Move gives Depleted, with a previously set trap and an opponent's attached Bond or Name. No effect if rear is unavailable.

cases.card_a: The King Had Given the Order
cases.reason: Swapping Bonds between already-Named formations preserves their Named state, so no completion trigger occurs.
cases.gameplay_decision: Bond swaps change exposed ongoing effects and position-based decisions without farming Name-completion bonuses.

cases.reason: The Tactic disables formation ACTION abilities and can remove Name Strength, not CONTINUOUS text. Iven's Tactic discount persists.
cases.gameplay_decision: Suppression of ongoing Name text is the distinct job of other opposing cards, such as They Returned With Names.

cases.reason: Continuous +1 Named Strength is included in provisional scoring before Stratagem eligibility. It can turn a tie into a lead and eliminate the tie branch.
cases.gameplay_decision: Choosing sustained Narratives versus keeping a close-result trap eligible is a real strategic tension.

cases.reason: Guarded prevents one affliction; No Step Back can prevent an Attack affliction or ignore a qualifying Tactic. Its reveal is optional, and spending both against one marker is usually wasteful.
cases.gameplay_decision: Preserve the difference between face-up renewable/multi-unit protection and a scarce concealed answer to a specific hostile effect.

cases.reason: Only one Stratagem card may be set per player each Battle; the same player cannot combine these reveals.
cases.gameplay_decision: The two Stratagems compete in deck construction and hand decisions. Opposing players may each use their own plan.

cases.reason: The Narrative ACTION gives Shaken to an Exhausted enemy without using the Archer's basic Attack. A counterattack via a pre-set Stratagem still needs a legal unused Archer Attack and an opponent's Attack trigger.
cases.gameplay_decision: This pair can coexist; the issue is tracking the Archer's Attack marker and timing, not a need to rewrite either card.
